newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Scitex in joint venture with German KBA.
newsitem.headline: Scitex in joint venture with German KBA.

text.p: Israel Scitex Corp said on Tuesday it had a signed a joint venture agreement with Germany's KBA Planeta AG to establish a new company for developing and marketing digital offset presses.
The new company will operate in Radebeul, near Dresden, and in Herzliya, Israel. Scitex did not disclose the amount to be invested in the joint venture.

"Their combined expertise makes them uniquely positioned to develop and support advanced systems that integrate digital workflows with a wide range of printing technologies," Scitex said in a statement.
Scitex, maker of pre-press, digital printing and digital video systems, has undertaken a massive restructuring of its graphic arts business in the wake of sharp losses of $4.16 a share last year.
It sacked 400 employees and took other measures to cut operating expenses by $10 million per quarter.
The result was a smaller-than-expected loss of $0.17 a share in the first quarter. Equity analysts predict the company will return to profitability by the third quarter.
KBA-Planeta, a subsidiary of KBA, manufactures medium and large size sheet-fed offset presses, dominating the large format sector.
Earlier on Tuesday, Scitex and Presstek Inc said they had agreement to cross-license certain technologies.
